HYB01YCA1U_C100.title: Large Frame
HYB01YCA1U_C100.description: DIOR MAISON X PIERRE YOVANOVITCH Dior Maison's collection of objects designed by Pierre Yovanovitch is the meeting of two stories. On one side, that of the Château de la Colle Noire, a property acquired by Christian Dior in the 1950s in the village of Montauroux in the Var countryside. On the other, that of the Château de Fabrègues, 65 km away, into which Pierre Yovanovitch has breathed new life for the last 10 years. Like Dior, who often stayed in the plains of Callian, Yovanovitch is also a child of the South, born in Nice, with strong ties to this region. In a sense, the collection, consisting of 15 objects including the large frame, is a reflection of this common southern anchorage. The design is 'simple, solid and noble,' as Dior defined his Colle Noire residence. Clean and functional, it celebrates the savoir-faire that Pierre Yovanovitch loves. The collection highlights traditional carpentry techniques and noble assemblies with local and sustainable materials selected for their beauty and timelessness. This collaboration is part of a story written by Dior Maison since the 1970s, featuring the greatest names in contemporary design, with Gabriella Crespi at the forefront. *Design by Pierre Yovanovitch for Dior
HYB01YCA1U_C100.characteristics:
85% oak wood, 10% glass, 5% cherry wood
Made in France

HYW01PPJ1U_C500.title: Decorative Wall Mural
HYW01PPJ1U_C500.description: Dior Maison reveals — for the first time — a new wallpaper adorned with Toile de Jouy. Dior Maison reimagines the signature motif as a non-woven wallpaper, reflecting an exceptional French savoir-faire. Its traditional fiber texture offers a unique effect, similar to linen. The exclusive and recyclable material revisits the emblematic drawings in a variation portraying wild animals, offered in delicate navy blue tones. A new invitation to enchant your interior with the House's timeless codes.
HYW01PPJ1U_C500.characteristics:
Recyclable high-end non-woven paper
PVC-based wall covering on paper backing
Solvent-free inks
Resistant to scratches and moderate contact
Washable
Quick dry time
Class A fire rating equivalent
Does not leave residue upon removal
Easy to install
Fast and careful shipment in rigid packaging
80% PVC, 20% non-woven paper
Made in France
Application of wallpaper and mural coverings:
Tools needed:
– Plumb line or level
– Pencil
– Adhesive for non-woven wallpaper
– Wallpaper smoothing brush
– Roller
– Box cutter
– Ruler
Before starting:
Make sure the wall is smooth, clean and dry. Sand any rough patches with the appropriate grit of sandpaper. Remove switch plates and outlet covers. They can be reintroduced following installation.
After placing the first length as straight as possible, use a level or plumb line. Trace a straight line 62 cm (24.5) from the edge of the wall and follow it for the first length of wallpaper.
Adhesive:
These wallpapers are non-woven, for which specific adhesives are made and solvent-free varieties are recommended. Prepare the adhesive as indicated in the product's instructions. Spread the adhesive directly on the wall with a roller or wallpaper brush.
Hanging:
Roll out the paper and begin at the top of the wall. If the wall is not straight, start from the higher side or allow the wallpaper to go 2 – 3 cm (1) over. Smooth the paper with the smoothing brush, moving toward the paper's edge to remove air bubbles. Cut the extra paper at the baseboards and ceiling with a ruler and box cutter. Use the roller on the length edges to make sure they do not curl.
